default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1518.title: Nested-box interior break fade
E-1518.hypothesis: A 10-minute box break that still sits far from both edges of the surrounding 60-90 minute box has not reached any level where the larger players rest orders; it is a rotation inside the bigger auction and the range traders of the large box lean against it, so fade it.

E-1519.title: Flat-open day box-break fade
E-1519.hypothesis: When the session opens almost exactly at yesterday's close, no overnight information needs to be priced and nobody arrives with urgent inventory; the day is run by intraday liquidity providers and a short box break has no initiator behind it, so fade it.

E-1520.title: Multi-day range contraction break fade
E-1520.hypothesis: When the last five sessions' average range is small next to the 20-session average, the market is in a multi-day compression where participants trade both edges and wait; intraday short box breaks in such a regime are rotations that get sold or bought back, so fade them.

E-1521.title: Light break-bar volume fade
E-1521.hypothesis: A close beyond the box made on a bar trading fewer contracts than the box's average bar is not an aggressor clearing the book, just thin quotes giving way; the resting size of the box is still there, so the break leans back inside; fade it.

E-1522.title: Inside yesterday's closing band break fade
E-1522.hypothesis: The range of yesterday's final minutes is where the last inventory was set and carried overnight; while price trades inside that band its holders are near break-even and defend it on both sides, so short box breaks there rotate back; fade them.

E-1523.title: Multi-session variance-ratio regime break fade
E-1523.hypothesis: A variance ratio below one over the previous 20 sessions (multi-bar returns smaller than the sum of 1-bar ones) shows the market has recently been dominated by liquidity providers whose quotes reverse moves; in that regime a 20-minute box break is reversed too, so fade it.

E-1524.title: Marginal-close break fade
E-1524.hypothesis: A bar that closes only a hair beyond the box edge (less than a fraction of the average bar range) shows the breakout side could not hold prices clearly through the level by the close; the stops are spent and the edge sellers (buyers) are still there, so fade the marginal break.

E-1525.title: Open-hugging day break fade
E-1525.hypothesis: When after the first half hour price is still close to the day's open versus the usual distance at this minute, the day has found no direction and the open acts as a magnet for both sides; short box breaks away from it are absorbed, so fade them.

E-1526.title: Spent range budget break fade
E-1526.hypothesis: Once the session range has reached most of the 20-session average daily range, day traders treat the day's travel as done and take profit at the edges while fresh initiators are scarce; a further short box break is met by that profit taking, so fade it.

E-1527.title: Minority-side break fade
E-1527.hypothesis: Counting the day's short box breaks on each side shows which side has been winning the session's auctions; a break on the side that has broken clearly fewer times is a counter-move into the dominant side's resting orders, so fade it, i.e. trade with the side that has been breaking more.
